idiom_name: ordered filter objects + filter chain + manager around a target
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a Filter abstraction with a single processing method that receives the request, the response and a handle to the rest of the chain; a FilterChain holds the ordered filters and exposes one call that advances to the next filter or to the target; a FilterManager (or the platform) selects and orders the filters for a request from a configuration or mapping and hands control to the chain. A filter performs its pre-processing, delegates unless it short-circuits, and then post-processes the response on the way back. Where the language has function values, the same structure is usually realised without classes: a filter becomes a function taking the next handler and returning a handler, and the chain becomes their composition.
pitfalls: A filter that neither delegates nor returns a response leaves the request hanging.
Sharing one filter instance across requests with mutable fields is a concurrency bug in any concurrent server.
The chain order and the mapping from request to filters are part of the contract; treating them as incidental configuration silently produces unguarded endpoints.

Wrong move: register authorization after a terminal or route-handling filter -> protected paths can run without the check -> instead place the guard before terminal handlers and assert the effective chain order.

Wrong move: mutate response headers or body after downstream output starts -> the protocol rejects late headers or produces a corrupted response -> instead set headers before delegation and wrap or capture the body where the framework supports it.

Wrong move: keep request data in fields on a shared filter or middleware instance -> concurrent requests leak state across one another -> instead use request-scoped context or local variables and keep the component stateless.
